questions.text: It's time to prepare the skit for the Teacher's Day assembly. What are you doing?

options.A: Standing near the stage, shouting directions, managing props, and telling the actors when to enter.
options.B: Researching exactly how much time each segment will take and creating a bulleted timeline for the teachers.
options.C: Writing the funniest dialogues and sneaking in the physics teacher's famous catchphrase to make everyone laugh.
options.D: Pitching the main theme to the Principal and deciding which students are best fit for which roles.

questions.text: You are posting a group picture from your friend's birthday treat at a fancy cafe. What is your role?

options.A: Directing everyone to make a fun reel, matching the text to the exact beats of the trending audio.
options.B: Adding the location tag, tagging all the brands you're wearing, and using the exact hashtags to get maximum reach.
options.C: Coming up with a killer, poetic, or hilarious one-liner caption that will get tons of fire emojis.
options.D: Planning the whole aesthetic of the post, telling friends not to post before you, and deciding the upload time.

questions.text: The school magazine needs entries. What are you submitting?

options.A: An energetic interview piece you did by talking to the Sports Captain on the football field.
options.B: A heavily researched, factual article on how AI and ChatGPT are changing board exams.
options.C: A short, emotional fictional story or a funny comic strip about the struggles of waking up for morning assembly.
options.D: You don't just write; you are the Student Editor deciding which articles make the front page and which get rejected.

questions.text: Your tuition group decides to pull a massive April Fool's prank on a friend. What's your job?

options.A: Briefing everyone on their specific cues and practicing the timing so no one breaks character.
options.B: Figuring out the logic—like how to safely hide their bag without them noticing the exact route you took.
options.C: Creating the fake backstory, drafting a hilarious fake warning letter, and making the lie sound super believable.
options.D: Overseeing the entire operation, assigning tasks, and making sure nobody gets caught by the tuition sir.

questions.text: A new street food stall opens near your house. How do you deal with it?

options.A: Going there with your squad, chatting with the bhaiya making the food, and hyping it up on a live video.
options.B: Checking Zomato for reviews, comparing prices with your usual spot, and analyzing if it's worth the hype.
options.C: Making a funny meme about 'Momos > Diet' and sharing it on your society WhatsApp group to tempt everyone.
options.D: Telling the stall owner how he can attract more college students by offering a 'Student Combo Deal'.

questions.text: For the Inter-House Essay Competition, what is your secret strategy to win?

options.A: Writing a speech-style essay meant to be read aloud with heavy drama, pauses, and hand gestures.
options.B: Structuring it perfectly with clear headings, bullet points, and verified historical dates to look super smart.
options.C: Starting with an emotional quote or a catchy story that instantly hooks the teacher reading it.
options.D: Analyzing the marking scheme first, then outlining the essay strictly to hit all the high-scoring criteria.

questions.text: Your colony is hosting the annual Diwali/Durga Puja function. What are you doing?

options.A: Holding the mic as the anchor, announcing the cultural performances, and keeping the crowd energized.
options.B: Designing the digital WhatsApp invite with the exact timings, Google Maps link, and parking instructions.
options.C: Writing a beautiful, dramatic script for the colony kids to perform a mythological play.
options.D: Sitting with the society uncles to finalize the event theme, the decoration budget, and the chief guest.

questions.text: You and your cousins are starting a YouTube channel. What is your main contribution?

options.A: Being the energetic host who moves around, talks to the camera, and records live reactions.
options.B: Looking at YouTube analytics to figure out exactly which titles, tags, and thumbnails will get the most clicks.
options.C: Writing the actual hilarious script, coming up with the jokes, and deciding the catchphrases.
options.D: Deciding the channel's niche, planning the upload schedule, and giving instructions to everyone else.

questions.text: You are fighting with a classmate over a WhatsApp group. How do you win?

options.A: Sending rapid voice notes to clearly express your tone, energy, and anger.
options.B: Digging up old screenshots and sending them as 'proof' to logically destroy their argument.
options.C: Crafting the ultimate, highly creative sarcastic reply that gets 'oooohs' from everyone else.
options.D: Taking control, de-escalating the drama, changing the topic, and ending the fight on your terms.

questions.text: Your dad asks you to help him write a complaint email to an airline for a delayed flight. What do you do?

options.A: Pacing around the room, dictating the words out loud to make it sound as urgent and angry as possible.
options.B: Organizing the email perfectly with PNR numbers, exact timestamps, and bullet points so they can't ignore it.
options.C: Using highly persuasive, slightly dramatic words to make the airline feel terrible and force them to give a refund.
options.D: Reviewing his rough draft, deciding it needs a completely different approach, and restructuring the whole strategy.

Event_Scriptwriter.title: The Stage Master (Event Scriptwriter / Playwright)
Event_Scriptwriter.primary_match_text: You love action, movement, and live energy! You don't just want words on a page; you want people to speak them out loud. As a scriptwriter for events, TV, or theater, you would coordinate with actors, manage stage directions, and bring stories to life in real-time.
Event_Scriptwriter.day_in_the_life: Your day is spent on sets or in auditoriums. You are writing dialogue, shouting cues, and making sure the host of a massive award show or a YouTube video knows exactly what to say to keep the audience cheering.
Event_Scriptwriter.alternative_match_text: If not Scriptwriting, you would excel as an Event Manager, Radio Jockey (RJ), or Film Director.
Event_Scriptwriter.roadmap: Take Arts/Humanities in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA in English Literature, Mass Media (BMM), or Performing Arts. Join college theater societies (Nukkad Natak/Dramatics). Diplomas in Screenwriting from FTII or Whistling Woods are highly valued.

Technical_Writer.title: The Information Hacker (Technical Writer / SEO Copywriter)
Technical_Writer.primary_match_text: You are logical, organized, and love making complicated things simple. You know how to play the system! In the professional world, you would be the writer who explains complex apps, gadgets, or software, and uses keywords to make sure articles rank number 1 on Google.
Technical_Writer.day_in_the_life: You sit with developers or product managers, understand how a new piece of technology works, and translate that into simple, bullet-pointed guides for normal people. You also track Google search trends to write articles that get millions of clicks.
Technical_Writer.alternative_match_text: If not Technical Writing, you would be a great Data Analyst, UX Researcher, or Tech Journalist.
Technical_Writer.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th (Science or Commerce with Math is a bonus). Pursue a BCA, B.Sc IT, or BA English. Get certifications in SEO (Search Engine Optimization), Google Analytics, and Technical Communication.

Ad_Copywriter.title: The Word Wizard (Ad Copywriter / Fiction Author)
Ad_Copywriter.primary_match_text: You are a creative genius with words! You know exactly how to make people laugh, cry, or click a button. In the advertising world, you would be the mastermind writing the catchy slogans on billboards, the funny scripts for Swiggy/Zomato ads, or gripping fictional stories.
Ad_Copywriter.day_in_the_life: You sit in a cool advertising agency brainstorming ideas over coffee. You come up with funny memes for brand social media accounts, write short Instagram reel scripts, and create taglines that millions of people will remember.
Ad_Copywriter.alternative_match_text: If not Ad Copywriting, you'd be a brilliant Stand-up Comedian, Author, or Social Media Influencer.
Ad_Copywriter.roadmap: Take Arts or Commerce in 11th/12th. Pursue a Bachelor of Mass Media (BMM), BA in Journalism, or BA English Honors. Build a strong portfolio of mock ads or a creative blog. Specialized ad schools or PG programs in Advertising are a huge plus.

Creative_Director.title: The Visionary Boss (Creative Director / Content Strategist)
Creative_Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader who sees the big picture. You don't just want to write the story; you want to decide what the story should be. As a Creative Director, you would manage teams of writers and designers, pitching massive campaign ideas to huge brands.
Creative_Director.day_in_the_life: You are in boardrooms pitching a Rs. 5 Crore Diwali ad campaign to the CEO of a huge company. Once they agree, you assign the writing, design, and video tasks to your team, overseeing the entire project until it goes live on TV.
Creative_Director.alternative_match_text: If not a Creative Director, you would be a powerful Brand Manager, Marketing Head (CMO), or Entrepreneur.
Creative_Director.roadmap: Take Commerce or Arts in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, BMM, or B.Com. The ultimate goal is to get an MBA in Marketing from a top B-School, or a specialized post-graduate degree from MICA (Mudra Institute of Communications, Ahmedabad), which is the gold standard for advertising in India.
